history.period: Legendary/ancient - no published founding date; present temple is a modern construction
history.summary: IDENTITY CONFIRMED: Anjan Dham in Anjan village (~18-21 km from Gumla via Toto, Palkot block) is the locally revered traditional birthplace of Lord Hanuman, named after his mother Goddess Anjani - it is also listed on the official Jharkhand Tourism website (destinationDetails/122). A cave at the site is believed to be the spot where Anjani gave birth to Hanuman; inside, a distinctive idol shows child Hanuman seated in Mother Anjani's lap (described as the only such temple in the country - verify). Tradition holds that Anjani bathed in a pond and worshipped Shiva daily, and the site is said to have 360 Shivalingas with an equal number of ponds; eight Shivalingas stand in two rows in the Chakradhari temple on Anjan hill, below which runs a long snake cave (Naga cave). Popular legend says the site's sanctity was 'discovered' by a Munda shepherd boy, that a British tehsildar ('William Saheb') helped build the temple, and that the Ratu Estate zamindar donated land and funds - all oral tradition, verify. The Munda and Oraon tribal priests (Pahan/Baiga) still manage rituals. Many archaeological objects found here are kept at the Patna Museum. Note: several other places in India (Karnataka, Maharashtra, Haryana) are also claimed as Hanuman's birthplace, so the claim is a traditional belief, not a settled fact. name: Anjan Dham
town_description: Gumla is the district headquarters town of Gumla district in the South Chotanagpur region of Jharkhand, about 90 km from Ranchi. The district is rich in tribal heritage (Oraon, Munda communities) and Nagvanshi history, with attractions including the Palkot Fort, Navratangarh (ancient Nagvanshi capital in Sisai block), Tanginath Dham (7th-9th century Shiva shrine), Hapamuni Mahamaya temple (11th century), and Anjan village - the locally claimed birthplace of Hanuman.

travel.airport: Birsa Munda Airport, Ranchi - about 130 km from Anjan Dham per Jharkhand Tourism (verify exact distance)
travel.railway: Nearest railheads are on the Ranchi-Lohardaga and Barkakana-Son Nagar routes; Ranchi Junction is the most reliable major station (verify nearest station)
travel.road: Anjan village is about 14-21 km off the Gumla-Lohardaga road via Toto (per tourism sources: 18 km via Toto, 130 km from Ranchi); concrete stairs and side footpaths lead up to the hilltop temple

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Ram Navami and Chaitra Navratri (March-April) see the largest crowds
